messages:
Ethan: Quick follow-up from todays all-hands  leadership asked us to distill the strategy into something AE/SEs can use. Can we get a 2	6 line boil-down + a couple of competitor rebuttals?
Kate (CEO): Boil-down: We help teams ship LLM features faster by removing inference ops risk: predictable latency, lower unit cost, and deployment flexibility (hosted -> dedicated -> private).
Nadia: Can we make that even tighter for pitches? Customers often cut to: why not just use cloud endpoints?
Samir: Quick pitch line: "Stop building inference plumbingstart shipping features. Redwood provides serving primitives, cost visibility, and migration paths so your team focuses on product not infra."
Priya: Add a one-sentence competitor rebuttal: vs managed cloud endpoints: "You get the primitives + cost transparency tailored for inference workloads, no re-architecting required." vs self-hosted: "You get the same control but without the initial 6-12 months of infra work."
Ethan: Nice. Can we include an objection handling bullet for "we can optimize on our own"?
Kate (CEO): Objection handler: "You can, but that work is often unrecoverable engineering debt. We deliver battle-tested batching, KV caching, and rollouts with measurable operational playbooks. For many teams that math favors buying instead of building."
Nadia: Any guidance on when to push Dedicated in the sales cycle?
Samir: Rule of thumb: when the customer projects steady peak qps above our reserved threshold OR compliance requires isolation. If theyre experimenting, stay Hosted. Also if latency SLOs require region colocation, propose Dedicated.
Priya: Marketing ask: can we surface a one-pager that maps buyer questions (cost, latency, compliance) to recommended deployment + expected timeline?
Kate (CEO): Yes  one-pager owned by Product Marketing. Keep timelines conservative: Hosted: days, Dedicated: weeks (capacity + SLA setup), Private: months (networking + compliance).
Ethan: Legal/quant ask: can we state expected cost savings in decks? sales wants a number to push deals.
Kate (CEO): No numbers without case-study signoff. Use qualitative language and two short customer vignettes until legal approves metrics. Route stats through GTM ops.
marketing-bot: Draft one-pager template created: https://redwood.internal/pm-marketing/one-pager-draft-1755555555 :memo:
Nadia: Thanks. Last thing  how do we track if this messaging reduces RFP churn? Any success metrics to monitor?
Samir: Track: conversion rate from POC to contract, average time to first production call, and frequency of migration requests from Hosted -> Dedicated. Tie these to quarterly goals.
Priya: I'll coordinate with analytics to add these funnels.
Ethan: Great, I'll synthesize the lines and objections and post a short doc in #product-playbooks. Thanks all.
